newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina to launch foreign share system on bolsa.
newsitem.headline: Argentina to launch foreign share system on bolsa.

text.p: Argentina's National Securities Commission announced the launch in September of Argentine Depositary Receipts (CEDEARs) that will allow local investors to trade in foreign shares on the Argentine bolsa.
When the system gets off the ground the bolsa will become the third stock market in Latin America where foreign shares may be sold or bought, after Mexico and Brazil.
Companies, banks or stock exchanges must have a net worth of at least $30 million to issue CEDEARs, the Securities Commission said in a statement.

The CEDEARs, in turn, will represent the stock of a single firm which must be listed on the bourses of Brazil, Uruguay, Paraguay or Chile, or else on a market with which the Buenos Aires bolsa has signed a specific memorandum of understanding.
